chester-le-street.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Chester-le-Street
s1loc: County Durham Foodbank runs its foodstore and distribution centre from First Avenue on the Drum Industrial Estate in Chester-le-Street, part of the Trussell network and managed by Durham Christian Partnership, with volunteers weighing, sorting and packing crisis parcels and chatting to clients over a cup of tea. On the high street, REfUSE runs its pay-as-you-feel community cafe, Durham's branch of the Real Junk Food Project, intercepting around twelve tonnes of surplus food a month that would otherwise be wasted across the North East.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities hold shops along Front Street with central buying behind them, while small community groups, the foodbank room and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across the town and its estates. St Cuthbert's Hospice has run its shop here since 1997, and Willow Burn Hospice shops sit nearby in Stanley. Larger charities order kit on trade accounts; the smallest want a handful direct online. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online, no minimum.

Beyond the foodstore and hospice shops, the town leans on a wider voluntary network. County Durham Volunteering brokers helpers into causes across the area, and REfUSE is run by a big family of volunteers from many backgrounds with a deliberately inclusive approach. St Cuthbert's Hospice fields seven retail shops and a furniture outlet across the county, raising over half a million pounds a year, while church-led pantries, warm spaces and lunch clubs run through winter around the Drum estate and Front Street. These volunteers all need hard-wearing, identifiable clothing.

wednesbury.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Wednesbury
s1loc: Black Country Foodbank serves Wednesbury and the rest of Sandwell's six towns, providing three days of emergency food to people in crisis while a longer-term solution is found. In the town itself, a community food pantry runs from Price Road Gospel Hall and the Breaking Bread Food Bank operates from Walsall Street, both volunteer-led. Sandwell Churches Link maps the foodbanks, pantries and community fridges across West Bromwich, Smethwick, Oldbury, Tipton, Wednesbury and Rowley Regis, and FareShare Midlands supplies surplus food to community groups right across the region.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities keep shops along the precinct and market with central buying behind them, while small community groups, the foodbank room and volunteer-run projects manage on a shoestring across Friar Park, Wood Green and Mesty Croft. FareShare Midlands redistributes surplus food to hundreds of community members, supplying the smallest groups. Larger charities buy kit on trade accounts; the smallest want a few direct online. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online, no minimum.

Beyond the foodbanks, the town leans on a wider voluntary network. The Friar Park Millennium Centre hosts community sessions and warm spaces, and church-led groups around Wood Green and Mesty Croft run lunch clubs and pantries through winter. Mary Stevens Hospice draws fundraising and shop volunteers from across Sandwell into its retail network, and charity-shop fronts for the heart and cancer charities sit near the market and bus station. Mutual-aid and faith groups collect food and household goods locally. These volunteers need durable, branded clothing they are recognised in.

denton.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Denton
s1loc: Willow Wood Hospice runs its Denton charity shop on Reddish Lane, one of six shops across Tameside and Glossop that, with a furniture outlet in Stalybridge and a distribution centre in Ashton-under-Lyne, help raise the millions the hospice needs each year with only a fraction coming from government. Tameside South and Longdendale Foodbank, part of the Trussell network, gets emergency food to people in crisis, and FareShare Greater Manchester redistributes surplus food to community organisations across the borough and East Cheshire.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities hold shops along Crown Point with central buying behind them, while small community groups, the foodbank room and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Haughton Green, Audenshaw and Denton West. FareShare GM, with over a hundred volunteers, packs orders for hundreds of charities and breakfast clubs. Larger charities order kit on trade accounts; the smallest want a few direct online. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online, no minimum.

Beyond the foodbank and Willow Wood shops, the town leans on a wider voluntary network. Feed My City works with partner organisations to get food to people across Tameside and the neighbouring boroughs, and Helping Hand Tameside connects residents with local support. Charity-shop fronts for the heart and cancer charities sit around Crown Point, while church-led pantries, lunch clubs and warm spaces run through winter across Haughton Green and Audenshaw. Mutual-aid groups collect and redistribute goods locally. Every one of these volunteers, from the foodbank sorter to the shop steward, needs hard-wearing, identifiable clothing.

port talbot.region: Port Talbot, Neath Port Talbot, Wales
port talbot.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Port Talbot
s1loc: Port Talbot Foodbank, part of the Trussell network, relies on the local community for donations, volunteering and finances, working a voucher referral system to get emergency food to people in crisis. The Bethel Trust, a registered charity on Sandfields Road in Aberavon, runs a foodbank, a food community shop, a baby bank and a Friendship Hub, all volunteer-led. FareShare Cymru, linked up with Neath Port Talbot Council for Voluntary Service, redistributes surplus food to local food banks and hubs across the area.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities keep shops along Station Road, with Cancer Research and Marie Curie among them and central buying behind them, while small community groups, the foodbank room, church pantries and volunteer-run projects manage on a shoestring across Aberavon, Sandfields and Margam. FareShare Cymru works with over a hundred and seventy organisations tackling hunger. Larger charities order kit on trade accounts; the smallest want a few direct online with no minimum. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online, no minimum.

Beyond the foodbanks and charity shops, the town leans on a wider voluntary network. Neath Port Talbot Council for Voluntary Service brokers volunteers into causes across the borough, and Home-Start Cymru supports local families through trained volunteers. The Bethel Trust adds a debt-recovery project and community church to its work in Aberavon, while church-led pantries, lunch clubs and warm spaces run through winter across Sandfields and Margam. Mutual-aid groups collect and redistribute goods locally. Every one of these volunteers needs durable, branded clothing they are recognised in.

aldershot.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Aldershot
s1loc: The Vine Centre on Station Road supports disadvantaged people across Rushmoor, running a Community Cupboard food pantry three mornings a week where people choose their own items and get budgeting and cooking advice. The Community Grub Hub, a community interest company set up in 2021 in the heart of Aldershot, runs a foodbank and community hub open every Tuesday with no referral needed. Rushmoor Voluntary Services manages the Rushmoor Volunteer Centre, recruiting and placing helpers into community projects across the borough.

National charities hold shops along Union Street with central buying behind them, while small community groups, the foodbank room, church pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across North Camp, Manor Park and Cargate. Rushmoor Voluntary Services backs the Princes Hall Foodbank and other small groups, and the Positive Change campaign channels giving to local causes. Charity-shop fronts for the heart and cancer charities sit around Union Street and North Camp, while church-led pantries and warm spaces run through winter. airdrie.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Airdrie
s1loc: Airdrie Foodbank, opened in 2014 and run by Calderbank Parish Church and its volunteers in association with the Trussell network, provides a lifeline of food, a listening ear and signposting to people in crisis across the local community. Volunteers weigh, sort and store donated food before packing parcels for clients to collect, and coordinate vouchers with referral agencies. It depends on the community for donations, volunteering and funding, and the Robertson Trust is among the bodies that have backed its work tackling the root causes of food poverty.

Hyndburn's Food Solutions Network has run a community conversation about food to ensure everyone in the borough can get what they need, working alongside the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks.
